Shares of neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius have already dropped 50% over the last three months amid concerns over AI debt. In this article APO Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT VIDEO 12:46 12:46 Watch CNBC's full interview with Apollo Global CEO Marc Rowan Apollo Global Management CEO Marc Rowan on Tuesday warned that neocloud companies could be in dire straits if Nvidia cuts off funding for their artificial intelligence projects. The chipmaker has become known as the "central bank of AI " due to the financing it provides to smaller companies like the neoclouds. Investors are now concerned that the funding could be slashed as Nvidia faces tougher scrutiny. "There was a strong incentive for Nvidia as a business matter to get these projects off the ground," Rowan said in an interview with CNBC's " Squawk on the Street ." "If that banking function, that guarantor function, gets taken away, access to capital for a large number of neoclouds is going to disappear." Nivida has been under pressure since CEO Jensen Huang stepped down Thursday amid an adultery scandal. The company is set to report earnings after the bell Tuesday under the leadership of interim CEO Colette Kress. Rowan's comments came after "Big Short" investor Steve Eisman told CNBC's " Squawk Box " Tuesday that the neoclouds " are all in big trouble because they are part of that vertical holding company and I think they're about to get ejected." Nvidia had $36 billion in off-balance-sheet AI cloud agreements, or backstops, for neoclouds, according to its last quarterly financial filing in July. Concerns about the massive amount of debt the neoclouds have taken on has already sent their stocks tumbling and bond yields rising. Bond yields move inversely to prices. CoreWeave and Nebius , which use the financing to build data centers, are each down more than 50% over the last three months. Stock Chart Icon Stock chart icon CoreWeave and Nebius year to date CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due in 2031 was yielding 15.66% on Tuesday, while spreads on its five-year credit default swaps hovered around 1,113.5. Credit default swaps are contracts in which investors pay for protection in case the borrower can't repay its debt. Wider spreads indicate investors view the bonds as riskier. Spreads over 1,000 are generally considered a sign of distress. CoreWeave's 9.75% bond due in 2031 on Nov. 17, 2026 If Nvidia decides to stop providing funding to neoclouds, the winners will be those companies that have the financial wherewithal and locked-in funding to build their infrastructure, Rowan said. That said, he believes new ways to secure funding will ultimately be developed in the AI space. "If you look back at other technology cycles, when Ford and GM introduced their first automobiles, people were amazed but no one could afford it. We ended up with GMAC and Ford Motor Credit," Rowan said. "We ended up with financial resources. It will not surprise me to see financial innovation take place, where more of a finance company mentality develops for this industry as an arbiter of credit and as a method of dealing with residuals," he added.
